text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":0.5,"launches":0.75,"pipeline":2,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Five evaluated points, all numerically passed, compiled, and saturating 32768 smem with 3 blocks/SM and identical 16.78 MB simulated DRAM. Latencies improved monotonically overall: 128x64x64/s1/sw0=234.82; 64x128x64/s1/sw16=235.12; 64x128x32/s2/sw16=221.79; 64x128x64/s1/sw8=214.47; 64x128x32/s2/sw8=203.69 (new best). Swizzle and simulated DRAM have never differentiated, so the analytic panel-reuse hypothesis is not materializing in traffic; traffic weight stays low at 0.5 and swizzle is kept open only to continue probing. Best points use block_N=128, so block_N remains narrowed to [128]; block_M stays [64,128] to keep the unsampled 128-M row alive; block_K [32,64] and stages [2,3] concentrate on deeper-pipeline variants since s1 points are all dominated. Pipeline weight held at 2 to keep steering toward the still-unsampled num_stages=3 regime (block_K=64 with s3 is untested), launches at 0.75 to favor larger/fewer tiles, footprint at 1 since every point saturates the cap and cannot differentiate. Hard 32768 portability cap retained. Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR; CUDA binary execution is not validated, and GB10 latency values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. Exploratory only; not a claim of global optimality."}
